status: frozen before computing the required harmonic field or cross-cluster boundary scores
purpose: Determine whether the cluster shear missing from AQUAL is a harmonic boundary field and whether measured baryons outside the scored strong-lensing region predict it with one transferable one-potential operator.

sample.target_interpretation: same-catalog conventional halo reconstruction used only as a spent inverse target, not direct truth

boundary_decomposition.interpretation: The shear generated by tapered missing convergence inside the analysis disk is the internal E-mode field. The remaining shear is the boundary candidate. Harmonic potential polynomials provide a target-derived upper bound, not a gravity model.

families.internal_only: five one-potential scalar features generated by baryons inside the scored 275 kpc disk
families.boundary_total: internal_only plus four exact shear fields generated by total measured baryons in successive outer annuli
families.boundary_components: boundary_total plus gas-minus-star outer-annulus fields, so total and contrast span separate gas and stellar boundary weights

fit.coefficient_rule: one real coefficient per one-potential feature; boundary features have zero convergence inside the scored disk and their shear orientation is fixed entirely by measured baryons
fit.alpha_selection: minimum symmetric leave-one-cluster-out full-field NRMSE across the two spent clusters
fit.final_diagnostic_fit: one joint coefficient vector on both spent clusters at the selected alpha

decision_rule: If harmonic modes m=2 through m=6 close at least half of the inferred boundary-shear power in both clusters, a boundary-like target component exists on the spent maps.

If measured outer baryons improve symmetric cross-cluster full-field NRMSE by at least ten percent over internal_only, reach NRMSE at most 0.5, align with the boundary shear by at least 0.5, and close at least 25 percent of boundary power in both transfer directions, require the next action to derive a covariant baryonic boundary propagator.

If the harmonic oracle passes but measured outer baryons fail, the target contains boundary structure not determined by the available projected baryon maps; obtain wider or line-of-sight environmental data before inventing a field carrier.
If the harmonic oracle itself fails robustly, do not pursue a static boundary mechanism; write dynamical-state postulates and enumerate velocity, shock, and relaxation data requirements.
No result in this spent stage validates a gravity theory or authorizes an untouched holdout.
claim_boundary: AS295 and PLCK G287 and their comparator maps are spent; this is mechanism discovery only.
The compact-halo comparator includes fitted external shear and is not direct pixel truth.
A finite-window internal/boundary split is not unique; padding sensitivity is therefore mandatory.
The registered baryon maps contain projected cluster-plane gas and stars but not all line-of-sight structure or matter beyond 1.8 Mpc.
Harmonic oracle coefficients are fitted separately to describe the spent target and are never theory parameters.
Outer-annulus regression coefficients and ridge penalties are inverse diagnostics, not proposed physical constants.
The one-potential construction is a two-dimensional integrability condition, not a four-dimensional covariant action.
